title: The Eisenhower matrix

source.author: Stephen Covey
source.work: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People

principle: Sort what's competing for your attention along two independent axes — how urgent it is and how important it is — instead of one. Urgent-but-unimportant items crowd out important-but-not-urgent ones by default, since urgency demands attention now; naming both axes explicitly makes it possible to protect the important, not-yet-urgent decisions.
formula: A purchase is urgent when urgency ≥ 2 and important when importance ≥ 2, giving four quadrants to sort the queue by.
fitsWhen: You have a growing list of things you might buy and need a quick way to separate what actually deserves priority from what's just loud.
critique: Urgency and importance are self-rated on a queue item, so the matrix is only as honest as the person filling it in — it doesn't correct for a tendency to mark everything as both urgent and important.
